newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds continue lower for second day.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds continue lower for second day.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed lower on Monday as the fall in CPI-linked bond prices triggered by the unexpectedly low April consumer price index continued, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 to 105.4
Volume including Makams was 138 million shekels.

"Yesterday there was a real craze for unlinked bonds. Today people are still looking to buy these bonds but the market is quieter because of the publication of the rise in money supply and the feeling that (the Bank of Israel) will lower interest rates only very slightly," said Dany Shamir of Israel Discount Bank.

April's 0.7 percent CPI rise, published on Thursday, was well below analysts' forecasts of about 1.1 percent. But M1 money supply rose a relatively sharp 2.3 percent in April, according to preliminary figures released by the Bank of Israel on Sunday.
The Bank of Israel will publish its key lending rate for June on May 26. The central bank last cut its interest rate to 13.9 percent at the end of February.

"The market does not expect the governor (of the central bank) to lower interest rates, but I believe he will lower the rate by 0.2 to 0.3 percentage point," said Adam Reuter, managing director of Financial Immunities consultancy.
There was excess supply of CPI-linked bonds today, but Shamir said demand was gradually resuming.

"Yields are attractive and traders are starting to see them as a buying possibility. Some traders are going back to buying CPI-linked bonds, while others are sitting on the fence waiting to see what happens in the market," he said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
